cycles.head: 7e036a9
cycles.verdict: CONFIRMED P1 BYPASS in the agent-PR bash guard. Attacked is_allowed_bash_command (agents_pr/guard.py:222) with 20 strings in-process, no commands run. 14/20 denied correctly - gh pr merge, gh api PUT merge, ;/&& chaining, $() substitution, git -c alias indirection, env prefix, case-folded MAIN, HEAD:main refspec, +refs/heads/main, --all, --mirror, --delete. THE BYPASS: _check_git_push compares branch.lstrip('+').lower() against {main,master,head}, so fully-qualified refs are not in the set. ALLOWED at HEAD: 'git push origin refs/heads/main', refs/heads/master, heads/main, refs/heads/HEAD, and the -u variant - while plain 'git push origin main' is correctly denied. Valid git pushing straight to main, defeating R10 'never merges'. Reachable via prompt injection since the agent works from attacker-writable GitHub issue text; blast radius bounded by AGENT_PR_ALLOWED_REPOS. Validated fix: strip leading refs/heads/ or heads/ before the comparison (blocks the bypass, still allows refs/heads/feature); better, require ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$. guard.py is not PROTECTED so an agent can fix it.

cycles.head: 7e036a9
cycles.verdict: MOST SERIOUS FINDING OF THE RUN - P1 credential exfiltration via an ALLOWED command. _UNSAFE_RAW_RE blocks $( and backticks but NOT bare $VAR, while claude_runner.py:160 puts the real credential in the agent env as GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN. Guard ALLOWS (executed): gh pr create --body "$GITHUB_TOKEN", --title "$GH_TOKEN", unquoted and ${...} forms, git commit -m "$GITHUB_TOKEN", git push origin "$GITHUB_TOKEN" - publishing the credential in a public PR body/title/commit. Agent instructions come from attacker-writable GitHub issue text. NOT EXECUTED and labelled as such: shell expansion at runtime is inferred, not observed - high confidence because the guard blocks $(, backticks, &&, ;, |, <, > which only matter under a shell. test_guard.py has no bare-$VAR case. Fix: _UNSAFE_RAW_RE = r'\$|`|\r|\n' plus tests. ALSO VERIFIED MY OWN CYCLE-12 MITIGATION CLAIM: check_repo_allowed is sound - 13 URL variants, all dangerous forms denied (userinfo injection, path traversal, lookalike host, query, fragment, ssh), deny-by-default when unset.

cycles.head: 7e036a9
cycles.verdict: FRONTEND INBOUND PATH. No XSS - verified zero dangerouslySetInnerHTML/innerHTML/outerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML/document.write anywhere in frontend/src/, so transcript text is React-escaped and cannot execute. NEW P2 data-channel-sender-unverified: room.ts:41's DataReceived handler checks topic and schema-validates via parseJarvisEvent but DISCARDS the _participant argument LiveKit provides to identify the sender, so any room participant can publish a forged {type:transcript,role:assistant} or {type:agent_state} on the jarvis topic and the SPA renders it as authentic. CHAINS WITH CYCLE 11: on the live deployment anyone can mint a token for any room with canPublishData:true, so a stranger can join a victim's room and forge what Jarvis appears to say. Filed P2 not P1 - content forgery, not code execution or exfiltration, and severity is carried by the already-filed anonymous-mode decision. Fix: match participant.identity or the SDK agent kind at the boundary that already filters topic and schema.

cycles.head: 7e036a9
cycles.verdict: P1 unauthenticated-cost-abuse: a public unmetered path to Hank's paid API spend. /api/token has no auth (cycle 11, executed) and NO rate limiting (grep over server/, pyproject.toml, fly.toml finds none). worker.py:176 has no agent_name so the SDK accepts every job - the repo itself records the worker 'auto-joining every load-smoke-* room'. Each session wires Deepgram+Anthropic+Cartesia (worker.py:153-155). Documented precedent: one 55-turn run exhausted a 20,000-credit/month free tier in ~13 minutes. DELIBERATELY NOT TESTED - creating rooms IS the harm; everything is code reading plus the repo's own recorded observations. TIMING IS THE POINT: Cartesia's 402 partly masks this today, and SUBMISSION.md step 1 is to restore those credits for the demo video, which re-opens the path exactly as the URL goes to graders. Options cheapest-first: take the app down after recording; set Clerk secrets; give the worker an agent_name (breaks the stranger-room-to-billing link on its own); rate-limit per IP. Recommended (1)+(3).

cycles.head: 7e036a9
cycles.verdict: P1 r3-inert-on-deployment: R3 'persistent cross-session memory' (a SPEC requirement and the first line of TECHNICAL.md) CANNOT be demonstrated on the deployed app, because every page load gets a new memory namespace. Chain verified: identityRef uses generateIdentity() = web-${Math.random()}; App.tsx never passes identity; NOTHING persists it (zero localStorage/sessionStorage/cookie/indexedDB in frontend/src/); anon mode's app.py:210 uses req.identity verbatim; memory/store.py scopes on user_id only. Within one page session memory works; across a reload - the definition of 'a new session B' in T-5's own acceptance - it cannot. Auth mode unaffected (app.py:185 never reads req.identity, uses verified Clerk user_id). T-5's resolved is legitimate; the gap is deployment configuration, not code. ON THE DEMO PATH: scripts/utterances/ ships memory-recall-preference.wav and memory-remember-celsius.wav. UNDOCUMENTED anywhere. Recommended fix: persist the anon identity in localStorage (small, agent-doable), or record with Clerk on - which also closes cycles 11 and 15, making it the highest-value single action available.

cycles.head: 7e036a9
cycles.verdict: FINAL TECHNICAL CYCLE - the last untouched surface: untrusted third-party text into the LLM. NO prompt-injection handling anywhere (every 'injection' hit is a dependency-injection seam) and the golden set has 0 adversarial cases (38 cases: grounded 17, refusal 14, memory 7). Two paths: (a) T-4 fetches LIVE GitHub issue/repo text into tool-result data, which ANSWER_POLICY calls 'the ONLY material you may draw on', with nothing distinguishing content-to-report from instructions-to-obey; (b) ANSWER_POLICY ends 'Honor every listed user preference exactly as written -- verbatim', and prefs come from mem0 keyed on the participant identity, which anon mode lets a client choose - so a planted preference inherits an obey-verbatim instruction. CLAIM: R6's 'zero fabrications' is evidence about COOPERATIVE inputs only - real, and narrower than it reads. NOT CLAIMED: that injection succeeds. DELIBERATELY UNTESTED - proving it needs a live paid model call and unprompted spend is inappropriate on the project whose Cartesia burn is why cycle 15 exists. Filed P2. Cheapest fix: a few adversarial golden cases plus an untrusted-content line in ANSWER_POLICY.
